analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: three CHANGELOG.md excerpts (head lines 1019-1796) and a docs/developer/build.md patch (hunk at @@ -1090,7 +1090,9 @@). No executable code, authorization logic, crypto, attestation, billing, or data-exposure paths change in the supplied units. Unit 9258958b65ed8e68:0 is a metadata-only entry with no text, so there is no further content to examine.

The build.md patch documents a new first runtime-smoke output line, `build-environment-runtime-smoke: <prod|dev> coordinator=<url> cdn=<url>`, and says the release workflow requires `<prod|dev>` to match the release environment. This is a build-environment binding for the release pipeline. It touches the A-005/A-011 release-registration area and the T-054 build-qualification area. The release workflow and the smoke-check source are not in the supplied batch, so enforcement of the match could not be verified. Out-of-scope release supply chain applies to the GitHub Actions/R2 pipeline.

The CHANGELOG entries mention many security-relevant features, including Stripe Global Payouts, an HF model-download fallback with hash verification, SSD prefix-cache defaults (100 GiB ceiling, 30-minute TTL per T-041), and profiler tables (T-051). They are prose only, and the corresponding source diffs are not supplied. I did not treat them as evidence of regressions. A later pass should check that the actual code matches these claims. In particular, the changelog says the shared SSD cache ceiling is 100 GiB, while T-041 says there is no fixed ceiling. This is a documentation discrepancy, not a vulnerability. Another thing to check is the new international payout route against T-030/T-060, and that the HF download path keeps its per-file SHA-256 and aggregate hash integrity checks.

No findings.
